feature.name: Odia Prawn Curry
feature.description: King prawns in a fiercely flavoured onion, ginger-garlic and chilli curry with freshly pounded cumin and coriander.
feature.note: Harden's named it one of the top five Indian dishes in London.

storyBand.imageAlt: A table of Potli dishes — paratha, curries, tandoori chicken and biryani
storyBand.heading: The chef's spice pouch, rebuilt on King Street
columns: Potli means pouch in Hindi. India's top chefs kept their secret spice blend in a small cloth pouch and took it away after cooking, so nobody could copy it.

Uttam Tripathy grew up in Sambalpur, Odisha, trained in Chennai, and opened Potli in 2011. Head chef Babul Dey has cooked here since the day it opened, grinding over 35 fresh spices daily. 2026 is our fifteenth year.

findUs.heading: 319–321 King Street
findUs.imageAlt: The Potli shopfront on King Street with pavement tables
findUs.body: Hammersmith, London W6 9NH — two minutes from Ravenscourt Park. There is pavement seating on King Street, so you can eat outside when the weather allows.
findUs.classesLead: Our chefs also run cookery classes — spices, three courses and a tandoor bread demonstration.
